ops.text: homeguard false-positives on any developer machine running the signed helper. internal/homeguard/homeFootprint digests the whole ~/.cc-notes tree, which includes ~/.cc-notes/fusekit-v1/catalog.sqlite plus its -wal and -shm sidecars. Those files are owned exclusively by the live CCNotesHelper daemon, which rewrites them on its own periodic catalog maintenance (catalog_maintenance_sequence/catalog_global_maintenance rows) with zero tenants provisioned and no test able to influence them. Any package guarded by homeguard.Main therefore FAILs after its tests already PASS, whenever a helper happens to be installed and running. Reproduced on clean origin/main d27331c: `./scripts/test.sh -count=1 ./internal/cli/` prints PASS then FAILs the package on "changed .../catalog.sqlite-shm" and "changed .../catalog.sqlite-wal"; an idle 20s window showed no writes, an ~80s test window did, matching a maintenance tick rather than anything the suite does. Suggested fix: digest the daemon-owned runtime dir by entry names/existence rather than content, so a test that creates or removes files there still trips the guard while a live daemon checkpointing its WAL does not. Deliberately not fixed inline: the fix trades away real guard coverage and belongs to whoever owns that tradeoff.
